usage.notes: ITK-Wasm can execute high-performance spatial processing in the browser, Node.js, Python and WASI environments. For Panacea web use, prefer worker-based asynchronous processing so large image operations do not block the React main thread. Local processing must remain possible without implicitly uploading patient data.

license.notes: Preserve applicable copyright, license and NOTICE obligations. Review third-party packages used by any selected ITK-Wasm pipeline independently before production integration.

validation.notes: A deterministic image-processing algorithm can be technically reproducible without being clinically validated for diagnosis. Panacea must validate each processing pipeline, parameters and derived measurement for its intended medical use.

provenance.notes: ITK-Wasm is currently in a 1.0.0 beta release series, so do not integrate an unpinned moving target. When activated, record the exact package/pipeline version, input artifact identity, voxel spacing, direction/orientation, coordinate system, parameters and output checksum for every derived artifact.

adapter.notes: Planned flow: PanaceaImagingStudy or PanaceaScientificVolume -> validated processing request -> worker-backed ITK-Wasm pipeline -> PanaceaImagingTransform with input IDs, algorithm/version, parameters, coordinate metadata and output checksum -> Cornerstone3D/vtk.js visualization. Processing results must never overwrite the immutable source study.

trust.notes: Scores describe engineering suitability for reproducible spatial processing. Clinical evidence quality still depends on the specific algorithm and intended use.
